Main.help: This \w allows you to configure your computers network connection.

gadgets.help: \Ssave your chosen setup. If you have altered your network settings, pressing Save may result in the temporary loss of your network connection until the computer is restarted.
AUN (Acorn Universal Networking) is the use of Econet protocols over Econet cable or Internet protocol networks. \Sconfigure the use of AUN.
Access is Acorns simple peer-to-peer networking system, that allows disc and printer sharing. \Sconfigure Access.
\Sconfigure your computer for use on a full TCP/IP Internet network.
\Squit the Internet configuration program without changing any network settings.
\Sdisplay interactive help.

This light indicates whether AUN is currently enabled.
This light indicates whether the TCP/IP Protocol Suite is currently enabled.

Internet.help: \TTCP/IP Protocol Suite configuration window. TCP/IP is the protocol used to access the global Internet.

gadgets.help: \Sconfigure the network interfaces fitted to your computer.
\Sset up the routing table for your network.
\Sconfigure your host name and name servers.

DNS.help: This dialogue box allows you to configure the Domain Name System for your network.

gadgets.help: Enter the IP address of the first name server to ask for a name lookups.
Enter the IP address of a second name server to try if the first does not respond. You may leave this field blank.
Enter the IP address of another backup name server. You may leave this field blank.
\Sapply the changes.

Enter the local domain of your machine here, if applicable.|MFor example, a machine on Acorns company network might be neptune.acorn.co.uk. That would give a Host name neptune and Local domain acorn.co.uk.
Enter the host name of your machine here. The host name you specify must be in your Hosts file.
\Suse only the local Hosts file to lookup host names.
gadgets.label: Use hosts file only

gadgets.help: \Suse a remote DNS server to lookup unknown host names.
gadgets.label: Use name servers also

Interfaces.help: This window shows the network interfaces fitted to your computer. If an entry is totally shaded, it is because there is no suitable driver in ROM or on disc.

Routing.help: This dialogue box allows you to set up routing information for your network.

gadgets.help: Enter the name of the default gateway machine for your network here. All non-local traffic will be initially routed to this machine if no other routing information is available.
\Sapply the changes.
\Sto make your computer forward IP packets between networks if you have more than one network interface.
gadgets.label: Act as an IP router

gadgets.help: \Srun the Internet routing module.|MClick MENU to change the RouteD settings.
gadgets.label: Run RouteD

gadgets.help: This icon is decoration only.

Interface.help: This dialogue box allows you to configure a network interface.

gadgets.help: \Sapply the changes.
Enter the IP address for this interface here. Use either dotted-decimal (eg 136.170.129.213) form, or a name in the Hosts file.
Enter the network mask for the network that this interface is connected to. Use either dotted-decimal (e.g. 255.255.248.0) or hexadecimal (eg 0xfffff800) forms. You may also specify "default".
\Sset the IP address of this interface manually in the writable field above.
gadgets.label: manually

gadgets.help: \Scontact a Reverse ARP (Reverse Address Resolution Protocol) server to find this interfaces IP address.
gadgets.label: via Reverse ARP

gadgets.help: \Sto obtain the IP address of this interface from CMOS RAM.
gadgets.label: from CMOS

gadgets.help: \Scontact a DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) server to find this interfaces IP address.
gadgets.label: via DHCP

gadgets.help: \Scontact a BOOTP (Boot Protocol) server to find this interfaces IP address.
gadgets.label: via BOOTP

gadgets.help: \Sset the IP address of this interface by looking up your host name in your Hosts file. This option is normally used in conjunction with the Primary interface option.
gadgets.label: from hostname

gadgets.help: \Sobtain the netmask for this network using an ICMP Mask Request message.
gadgets.label: ICMP

gadgets.help: \Smake this interface the "primary" interface. Some third-party applications may only use the primary interface.
gadgets.label: Primary interface

gadgets.help: \Sclose the dialogue box without applying any changes.

\Sto set the RouteD options.
